subtopics.title: The Question, the Population and the Sample

questions.question: A research question sharp enough to investigate must name:
options: The group, the quantity and the unit
The graph that will be drawn

questions.question: For a survey about the school's 1 240 learners, the population is:
options: The grade 11 class doing the survey

questions.question: Surveying 60 of your own grade 11 friends about weekly spending is biased because:
options: Sixty is too small a number for any survey
Seniors carry more pocket money than juniors, so the sample tilts away from the school's truth

questions.question: A random sample is one where:
options: Learners are chosen for being easy to reach
Every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen

questions.question: The frequency of a group in a tally table is:
options: The count of strokes recorded for that group
The middle value of the group
The sum of the rand amounts in it

questions.question: Class intervals written as 'R20 to R40' followed by 'R40 to R60' are faulty because:
options: A learner spending exactly R40 has two possible homes — the intervals overlap
The second interval should come first

questions.question: The frequencies 8, 19, 21, 7 and 5 are checked by:
options: Adding them — the total of 60 confirms every learner was counted exactly once

questions.question: The price paid for grouping data into intervals is:
options: The table becomes longer than the raw list
The frequencies stop adding to the total
The exact values are lost — detail is exchanged for shape

subtopics.title: Mean, Median, Mode and the Story of the Range

questions.question: For the sorted data 20, 25, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 90, the mean is:
options: R40, from a total of 360 divided by 9

questions.question: The median of those nine values is:
options: R35 — the fifth value, with four below and four above

questions.question: The mean sits above the median in this dataset because:
options: The R90 outlier drags the mean upward, while the median only cares about position

questions.question: If the mean of nine values is R40, the total of the values must be:

subtopics.title: Graphs That Tell the Truth — and Graphs That Lie

questions.question: The right graph for comparing boys' and girls' average spending per grade is:
options: A multiple bar graph with the bars side by side and a key

questions.question: A scatter plot of airtime spending against pocket money, with dots climbing to the right, suggests:
options: More pocket money tends to go with more spending

questions.question: The three-step discipline for reading any graph is:
options: Values first, then the title, then the colours
Title and axis labels first, the scale second, the values last
Count the gridlines and divide by two

questions.question: A vertical axis starting at R35 instead of R0 makes a R40 bar tower over a R36 bar. The defence is to:
options: Assume the taller bar is triple the shorter
Read the numbers off the axes and quote them against the picture — the difference is only R4

subtopics.title: Asking the Right People the Right Question

questions.question: 'Do learners waste money on data?' fails as a survey question because:
options: 'Waste' is an opinion — the question must ask for a countable quantity with a unit

questions.question: A census was rejected for the school survey because:
options: Asking all 1 240 learners is accurate but too slow and expensive for the deadline
Censuses only work for whole countries

questions.question: Taking every twentieth name on the alphabetical register is a way of:
options: Giving every learner an equal chance, so no one's convenience chooses the sample

subtopics.title: Sixty Answers into One Small Table

questions.question: Amounts from R0 to R120 are tallied into bins rather than single values because:
options: Nearly every separate value would score one stroke, revealing no shape
Tallies only work with round numbers

questions.question: The bins say 'R20 to under R40' with the next starting AT R40 so that:
options: The bins can have different widths
Every amount has exactly one home — a R40 spender cannot live in two bins

questions.question: What the finished table can NOT tell you is:
options: How many learners spend R80 or more
Which bin holds the most learners
The exact biggest amount — the table knows five spent R80 or more, not that one spent R120
Whether all sixty slips were counted

subtopics.title: Three Middles, One Spread, and a Graph with a Trick

questions.question: The share-out picture of the mean says:
options: Pool all the money — R360 — and share it equally: R40 each
Tap the middle shoulder of the queue
Measure the gap from smallest to biggest

questions.question: The median 'never met the R90' because:
options: It only counts positions in the queue — the middle does not care how rich the last person is
The median is always smaller than the mean

questions.question: The range of the dataset 20 to 90 is:
options: R70 — the gap from smallest to biggest, a spread not a middle

questions.question: The axis check performed before trusting any graph is:
options: Measuring the bars with a ruler
Asking where the vertical axis starts — a start at R35 dresses a R4 difference up as a landslide
